messages:
alex: heads-up — staging private deploy failed the isolation smoke tests after the latest netpol changes. pods in the inference sandbox can still reach the ops-mgmt CIDR :thinking_face:

maria: :eyes: which rule slipped? I thought we had deny-by-default on ingress + egress for the tenant namespaces

isaac: saw this in CI logs. Looks like the eBPF agent we rolled last week is still letting ARP/neighbor probes through, which our virtual firewall interprets as allowed egress. reproducer in the log below.

sec-ci-bot: CI Pipeline #4921: network-smoke-test failed (netpol-apply -> smoke-test). See artifacts: https://ci.internal/reports/4921

linda: can you paste the failing line? also tag devops for the eBPF agent reference @devops

isaac: sure — relevant excerpt: ```
[2024-03-03T14:21:03Z] pod=inference-qp-7f6 netns=/var/run/netns/xyz proto=arp op=request dst=10.0.200.1 src=10.0.4.12 verdict=ALLOW via-ebpf
```

alex: that `verdict=ALLOW via-ebpf` is the problem. we expect the eBPF policy to return DROP for cross-tenant ARP/neigh across the tenant-subnet boundary.

maria: quick checklist: 1) RBAC — did we grant the eBPF agent clusterrole too wide access when we updated? 2) KMS — do ephemeral KMS bindings the agent uses allow it to fetch broad network policies? 3) Audit logging — did syslog forwarder include the agent decisions for later forensics?

devops: for RBAC we scoped `netfilter-agent` clusterrole to namespace `infra-system` only, but the pod we deployed ended up in `infra-system-staging` due to helm chart value mismatch. that explains the broader reach.

linda: oh wow, helm value bug. can we patch to strictly `infra-system`? and rotate the service account tokens for the old SA?

isaac: yes patch ready: ```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: netfilter-agent-binding
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: netfilter-agent
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: netfilter-agent-sa
  namespace: infra-system
```

alex: rotate tokens + revoke existing SA creds in KMS. for Private (on-prem) we use KMS proxy with ephemeral bindings — we should invalidate existing bindings and issue new short-lived certs. isaac, can you add the revoke step to the patch?

isaac: added. Also flagged a potential CVE in the eBPF userland binary (OpenSSL dependency) — triage ticket created: SEC-TRIAGE-178. CVE-2024-0xxxx — low/medium impact but worth updating the package.

maria: good catch. schedule vuln patch for next maintenance window. also we need to ensure audit logs contain both pre- and post-decision snapshots for network decisions. right now auditd forwards only accept/deny, not the matched selectors. ops: can we capture selectors? @sre_oncall

sre_oncall: we can, but will increase log volume. approach: sample 1% of flows with full metadata, and keep full metadata for any flow crossing tenant boundaries. writeup: ```
- sample_rules: 1%
- full_capture: cross-tenant=true
- retention: 90d meta, 365d hashes
```

devops: syslog-forwarder already supports structured JSON, we just need to enable the `ebpf_decision` field. i'll add a flag and ship a canary to staging.

linda: for incident response: recommend a tabletop on Friday to walk through revoke + krash scenario. Include PSIRT, infra, and legal. we should rehearse: 
1) revoke SA creds in KMS
2) apply strict netpol patch
3) force rolling restart of agent pods
4) verify via smoke tests and sampled logs

alex: agree. can we also add a fallback: when netpol verification fails, route traffic to a blackhole service (reject at LB) rather than letting eBPF fallback to permissive? this would be a safer default for private deployments.

isaac: that's feasible — implement a `network-fail-closed` ConfigMap for the agent. quick snippet: ```yaml
data:
  fail_mode: CLOSED
  blackhole_service: kube-system/blackhole
```

maria: two more items: 1) KMS audit trail must show who requested token revocations, and 2) update onboarding docs so infra teams know the exact namespace values (to avoid helm value mismatch).

sec-ci-bot: Action items created: NETPOL-789 (apply RBAC patch), KMS-502 (revoke bindings), TRIAGE-178 (ebpf vuln), IR-2024-03-08 (tabletop).

linda: i'll own NETPOL-789 and the tabletop invite. devops owns KMS-502 and TRIAGE-178. isaac will validate smoke-test after patch.

alex: thanks all. let's not block the Dedicated customers — apply the patch to staging first, monitor, then schedule private clusters. :shield:
